**Comment**
+1 to add. The appropriate SPDX license expression in my eyes would be (BSD-3-Clause-Clear AND AOMPL-1.0). In my eyes they apply to different aspects. Perhaps we find the opportunity to discuss this item. In particular, the BSD-3-Clause-Clear makes an explicit statement, that patents are not covered.

While Fedora has resolved this (by using `Addition-Ref-`) - we probably should discuss whether to add this to SPDX License List in any case. I can see why Fedora landed on `WITH Addition-Ref-`, but could also see @karsten-klein point re: it being used with `AND` as it reads like its own standalone license. 
Given its used widely and meets the general concepts of the various free/open license definitions if you overlay those for the scenario of an implementation of a specification, I am currently leaning towards it being eligible to add. However, I believe this would be a first for adding a specific patent license (that doesn't seem to also include a copyright license)

Thoughts??

@jlovejoy I don't see how `AND` is appropriate, because the patent license covers the same stuff as the hypothetical software license (and would never appear in a FOSS repository without there being an accompanying software license). `AND` is (as I see it) for situations where one license covers some discrete portion of code and another license covers some other discrete portion of code. This is why Fedora used `AdditionRef-`. These patent licenses which you occasionally see in FOSS-ish repos are arguably analogous to license exceptions (additional permissions). 

Adding this as a standalone license would also seem to have implications for the past interest in getting things like the various Google project separate patent license grant statements added to the SPDX list.

I tend to agree with @richardfontana here (and the various forms of Google patent license grants came to mind for me as well).

This has come up frequently enough now that we should probably make a policy decision about how to handle these sort-of-but-not-really-standalone patent licenses. My personal thoughts are:

1. They shouldn't be included as a 'license' on the main [SPDX License List itself](https://spdx.org/licenses), to be used as an `AND` in an expression. Primarily because (in my view) anything that is a 'license' on the main License List should be able to be used on its own as a license for software (or documentation, or data, etc.), and a pure patent license doesn't work in that way.
2. I'm starting to lean towards, let's just put it on the [SPDX Exceptions List](https://spdx.org/licenses/exceptions-index.html) as an 'additional permission' as @richardfontana mentioned. It would then be usable in a `WITH` exception.

I've been resistant to option 2 in the past (e.g. [here](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/646#issuecomment-569969690)), mostly out of taking a fairly purist view that if it's an exception / additional permission, it should be possible to strip away the exception and use it under just the base license alone. And that, in the case of something like e.g. `BSD-3-Clause WITH Google-patent-grant`, there's an argument that the _explicit_ additional patent grant changes the meaning of any _implicit_ patent grant that might otherwise exist in BSD-3-Clause standing alone.

But as time has gone on, I am starting to think that it is unhelpful to the community to exclude these "FOSS-ish" patent grants from being _somewhere_ on the License / Exception List, if they're being accepted in practice in FOSS-based distros and communities. Probably better to add them so that they can be talked about in a unified way, rather than expecting the ongoing use of `AdditionRef-` with different IDs by different FOSS communities.

And to be clear, I'm talking only about adding these clearly-compatible-with-FOSS patent grants; not every standalone license and not e.g. additional restrictions.

@jlovejoy If you're aligned with this, perhaps I can create a separate issue where we can discuss and get alignment on a few basic criteria for adding to the [License Exception Principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md#license-exceptions) to address how we would think about these? I think there's a few things we could call out. From a quick thought, e.g. cannot require royalties / RAND; perhaps something like that it must be generally compatible with royalty-free distribution of software consistent with OSD requirements and principles; etc. I'm guessing we can build this out further in a separate issue if you're aligned that it would be helpful to go this direction.

agree with @swinslow and @richardfontana comments above, including the rationale for adding this (or things like it) to the exception list. We may other open issues similar to this one, so would be good to come to a conclusion so we can move on!
OK with a policy change - as Steve says, it allows these add-ons to be corralled under a consistent ID.
this has been open and tagged with "discuss" for some time. Let's actually make a plan to discuss on the next call on Jan 22nd

discussed on Jan 22nd call (@swinslow @jlovejoy @karsten-klein ) 
- clarification on use of `AND` in response to @richardfontana 's comment above: use of `AND` can be for a situation as you describe, but also where two license apply to the same code. It is not as narrowly defined as your description above. Consider that `AND` can be used in a license expression applying to a file or an entire package
- <<question of if add - is it a license or exception and does it meet the guidelines>>
Reiterating that I like this as an exception/additional grant rather than a standalone per @richardfontana & @swinslow.
I see that #2613 was added to the exception list could this also get an approval of getting added to that list? Or is there anything else blocking this?
